_meta.purpose: Operational manifest for keeping the dead-detained-deported hypergraph current. Each entry's id matches a source node in the hypergraph itself, so the update system and the topology describe the same objects.
_meta.pipeline: update_pipeline.py — `status` shows staleness, `fetch <id> --network` refreshes one source layer (network access only on explicit request), `rebuild` merges all layers into the canonical file.
principles: Snapshots are append-only: raw fetched bytes are saved dated under snapshots/ before any parsing, so extraction is always re-runnable and no information is ever lost to a parser bug.
One source = one layer file under layers/. A refresh regenerates only that layer; merge-by-node-ID federates the layers into the canonical file.
Deterministic IDs (ddd_lib slugs) make re-extraction converge on the same nodes, so merges dedupe instead of duplicating.
Nothing is deleted on update. If a source drops a record, the record stays in its last layer with its extraction timestamp; corrections surface as i2t:conflicts entries, never as silent overwrites.

sources.latency: Statutory 90-day reporting window; interim notices within 2 business days of a death.
sources.coverage_gap: Excludes deaths after release/parole and deaths during street-level enforcement operations.

sources.access: web-portal; bulk feeds via academic agreement
sources.latency: 30-60 day reporting lag; depends on FOIA enforcement lawsuits.
sources.coverage_gap: PII redacted (names, A-Numbers); aggregate and record-level only.
sources.notes: Detention-statistics tables update monthly. A fetcher would target the ADP and facility tables and emit metric edges on system:ice-detention-network.

sources.latency: Batch releases following federal court orders; quarterly to semi-annual.
sources.coverage_gap: Anonymized internal identifiers only; no names.
sources.notes: The richest microdata: arrests, book-ins, transfers, flight manifests, linkable across years by anonymized id. A fetcher would emit EnforcementAction-style state-change edges and facility nodes.

sources.access: REST API + webhooks (free tier available, token recommended)
sources.coverage_gap: Only detainees who secure representation and file federally.
sources.notes: Query ideas: new 2241 habeas petitions naming ICE; dockets citing withholding orders. Unsealed filings carry real names and named facilities — the de-anonymization bridge between DDP microdata and persons.
Best source for facility geocoordinates — the map layer of the infographic.

sources.access: manual search only — CAPTCHA-gated, no API; requires exact A-Number+country or name+DOB+country
sources.coverage_gap: Post-2026-09-15, deliberately returns empty for ~16,000 final-order detainees.
sources.notes: NOT scrapeable (anti-automation by design). Recorded here because its silences are themselves data: a person findable last month and unfindable now is a signal event the graph can represent.
